messages:
nate: FYI I hit a regression in the slot allocator and it looks like head-of-line blocking when the batch coalescer tries to merge a bunch of long-context requests. Tail latency 95/99 jumped 2-3x under sustained chat load. attaching quick notes.

maria: can repro with our longctx harness. queue depth climbs, one request sits at head for ~200ms. repro script: `stress_longctx.sh --parallel 200 --seq 2048` :grimacing:

priya: captured pprof and a flamegraph. key stack repeated:
```
redwood/runtime/cache/slot_allocator.go: WaitForSlot
redwood/runtime/batcher/coalescer.go: mergeBatches
redwood/runtime/kv/fragment_copy.go: copyFragments
```
Counters: slot_waits=412k, avg_wait_ms=18.2, merge_aborts=42
Flame: https://internal-tools/redwood/flame/3735554321.png

lee: initial read: merge path holds the head lock while doing fragment list copying -> any slow copy stalls whole queue. two quick ideas:
  1) release head lock before copy and re-check invariants (racy but safe if refcounts)
  2) lower merge threshold (8 -> 4) so coalescer chooses faster merges

nate: lowered threshold locally: 95th latency -30% but mean CPU rose for small requests. tradeoff is visible. also saw fragmentation increase over long runs; reuse rate drops and GC not reclaiming pinned fragments.

priya: propose adaptive merge heuristic: use oldest-request-age + slots-in-flight to decide merge. pseudocode:
```
if oldest_age > AGE_LIMIT or slots_occupied > SLOT_HIGH: disable_merge()
else if queue_len >= MIN_MERGE: enable_merge()
```
This avoids merging when a request is already waiting too long.

maria: also tracing shows fragment pin refs linger when merge aborts happen; that explains memory growth for long-context sessions (24h drift). I'll bisect where pinned refs are not dropped on abort.

nate: can we run a canary with the adaptive heuristic + instrumentation on dedicated-gpu-pool-3? want to watch slot_waits, merge_count, pinned_fragments, tail latency.

lee: I'll draft a small PR with metrics and the adaptive switch behind a feature flag. will also add a metric for copy_time_ms so we can threshold fast-path vs slow-path.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started to dedicated-gpu-pool-3 (deploy id c2678). monitoring channel: #canary-dedicated-3

priya: will push a prototype binary with the flag set to off by default. plan: enable for 2 hours, check 95/99 and pinned_fragments.

maria: note: also test eviction pressure scenario. if eviction runs concurrently with merges we might see extra fragmentation. add a synthetic evicter load in the harness.

nate: agreed. schedule a short sync after the canary results. thanks all :thumbsup:
